links.outcome: Factuality and completeness of responses; relevance of retrieved passages and evidence selection
links.effect: Factuality and completeness dropped by up to 6% and 5% vs non-RAG; only 22% of top-16 passages relevant; evidence selection precision 41-43%, recall 27-49%
links.tradeoff: Standard RAG introduced a new failure mode: poor retrieval and evidence selection that contributed to the overall performance drop.
links.quote: Contrary to expectation, standard RAG often degraded performance: only 22% of top-16 passages were relevant, evidence selection remained weak (precision 41-43%, recall 27-49%), and factuality and completeness dropped by up to 6% and 5%, respectively, compared with non-RAG variants.

links.effect: Improvement of up to 12% on MedMCQA and up to 8.2% on MedXpertQA (reported jointly for evidence filtering and query reformulation)
links.quote: We further show that simple yet effective strategies, including evidence filtering and query reformulation, substantially mitigate these issues, improving performance on MedMCQA and MedXpertQA by up to 12% and 8.2%, respectively.

links.comparator_used: standard RAG using the original query
